title: A Bag of Tricks for Defending Deep Learning-based Face Recognition Pipelines against Backdoor Attacks
abstract: arXiv:2611.06412v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The protection of mature, multi-stage Face Recognition Systems is crucial to system providers. This technical report targets the threat model most relevant to industry practitioners: although model training is performed in-house, training data is sourced from possibly-compromised third parties. Given this setting, we present three practical defense "tricks" against data poisoning-based backdoor attacks. The first operates at training-time, detecting poisoned identities during training or prior to a pipeline's deployment. The last two operate at inference-time, filtering suspicious inputs before an answer can be sent back to a potential attacker. Each method is presented with their motivation, algorithms and computational impact, and evaluated on realistic face recognition workloads. Our goal is to provide actionable hardening techniques to system providers.

translated_title: 《防御基于深度学习的人脸识别流水线免受后门攻击的一揽子技巧》
translated_abstract: 本技术报告针对与行业从业者最相关的威胁模型：尽管模型训练在内部完成，但训练数据来源于可能已被入侵的第三方。在此背景下，我们提出了三种针对基于数据投毒的后门攻击的实用防御“技巧”。第一种在训练阶段运行，可在训练期间或流水线部署之前检测被投毒的身份。后两种在推理阶段运行，在将结果返回给潜在攻击者之前过滤可疑输入。每种方法都介绍了其动机、算法和计算开销，并在真实的人脸识别工作负载上进行了评估。我们的目标是为系统提供商提供可实际操作的加固技术。
tldr: 本文针对训练数据可能被第三方污染的人脸识别系统，提出了三种实用的后门攻击防御技巧——一种在训练阶段检测被投毒的身份，两种在推理阶段过滤可疑输入，为系统提供商提供了可落地的安全加固方案。
en_tdlr: This paper presents three practical defense tricks—training-time poisoned identity detection and two inference-time suspicious input filtering methods—against data poisoning backdoor attacks in face recognition systems whose training data may come from compromised third parties.
